series: Things Living In Your House, Part 7
sources: University of Kentucky Entomology, Bed Bugs (ENTFACT-636, M. Potter): adults about 3/16 inch, reddish-brown, oval and flattened; fit into crevices no wider than a toothpick; active mainly at night; the bite is painless and a blood meal takes about three to ten minutes; nymphs and adults persist months without feeding, up to about a year at 55 F or cooler; females lay one or more eggs a day, hundreds in a lifetime; eggs about the size of a dust speck; nymphs molt five times and need a blood meal between each molt; disease transmission to humans not proven and considered unlikely; hide in mattress seams, box springs, bed frames, headboards; https://entomology.mgcafe.uky.edu/ef636
US EPA, Bed Bugs: Appearance and Life Cycle: adult about the size of an apple seed; https://www.epa.gov/bedbugs/bed-bugs-appearance-and-life-cycle

US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, About Bed Bugs: 1-7 mm; not known to spread disease; bite at night while people sleep; stay near where people sleep; spread by hiding in luggage, bags, folded clothes and furniture; https://www.cdc.gov/bed-bugs/about/index.html

University of Kentucky College of Agriculture news, UK entomologists help sequence bed bug genome: traumatic insemination, 'a male pierces the female's body and deposits sperm into her body cavity'; https://news.mgcafe.uky.edu/article/uk-entomologists-help-sequence-bed-bug-genome

Wang et al. 2009, Journal of Economic Entomology (hosted by Purdue Extension), bed bug pitfall traps: carbon dioxide and heat both attract bed bugs, CO2 more strongly; https://www.extension.entm.purdue.edu/bedbugs/pdf/BedBugTrap.pdf

title: Bed Bugs Drink Your Blood While You Sleep 🩸
tiktok_caption: bed bugs drink your blood for up to ten minutes and you never feel it 🩸 then they mate by stabbing. Would you check your mattress tonight? 🔦 yes / 🙈 never

beats.say: Right now, something in your bed is waiting for you to fall asleep.
The bed bug. Flat, reddish brown, about the size of an apple seed.
By day, it hides in the seams of your mattress.
At night, it follows your breath. The carbon dioxide you breathe out.
Then it bites, and drinks your blood for up to ten minutes.
And you never feel a thing.
Its bite is painless, so you just keep sleeping.
The babies need a full blood meal before every single growth stage.
Five stages. Five meals. All of them, you.
A female lays eggs every day. Hundreds in her life. Each one the size of a dust speck.
Now the gross part. The male doesn't mate the normal way.
He stabs straight through her body, and injects his sperm inside.
Scientists actually call it traumatic insemination.
And starving them out doesn't work. In a cool room, they can wait about a year without eating.
The good news? They're not known to spread disease. Just itchy bites.
They ride home in luggage and folded clothes.
Would you check your mattress tonight?
Sleep tight. Something in there is counting on it.
Follow me. Part eight lives in your kitchen.
